Scene: the originally roofed arcaded loggia at Upper Barrakka, Valletta, overlooking Malta's Grand Harbour, in the eighteenth century before its roof was dismantled in 1775. This is an explicitly approximate architectural interpretation of a lost covered space, not a photograph of its present state or a claim to an exact documented roof reconstruction.
Primary subject: a completely empty, shaded limestone arcade with the ENTIRE roof still in place above the passage. Repeated sturdy honey-colored Maltese limestone piers and rounded arches support a continuous understated plain flat ceiling. The ceiling must be visibly closed and unbroken from the foreground to the far end: absolutely no open sky above the passage, no missing roof, no uncovered pergola. Keep the approximate ceiling simple; no ornate coffering, no Gothic ribs, no invented monumental barrel vault, no modern roof panels or metalwork.
Composition/framing: eye-level camera looking lengthwise along the covered arcade, a strong but natural receding perspective, full 3:2 landscape frame. Show the overhead ceiling clearly in the upper third and weathered plain stone paving clearly below. The passage leads to daylight at its distant end. Through the open arches along the harbour-facing side, and ONLY through these arches, show a modest band of blue Grand Harbour water, a narrow hazy skyline and low period limestone bastions of the opposite shore. No modern city, port equipment or vessels. The harbour remains a secondary glimpse through the architectural openings; the covered stone arcade is the dominant subject.
Style/medium: convincing camera-captured photograph-like historical illustration, solid and spatially plausible limestone architecture, gently aged limestone with subtle pores, joints and small irregularities, matte stone slabs underfoot. Natural warm Mediterranean daylight entering from the side arches creates soft-edged curved patches of light and shadow across the stone floor, with softly lit shaded arches and ceiling; understated muted honey-beige stone and moderate natural blue water. Retain readable detail in the shade without HDR. No theatrical light beams, no cinematic grading, no artificial glow, no oversaturation, no glossy CGI.
Constraints: zero people or animals. No tourists, benches, furniture, statues, plaques, inscriptions, signs, modern buildings, lift, electric lights, pipes, cables, railings, machinery, cranes, ships, boats, cars or contemporary objects. No text, letters, digits, emblems, logos, watermark, caption, image frame or border. No violence. The scene is only the empty fully roofed historical limestone arcade and distant harbour glimpses through its arches.

Asset type: historical architecture educational illustration for the Valletta city introduction.

Scene and subject: an original approximate architectural interpretation of the CENTRAL EXTERIOR FACADE of Auberge de Castille, Valletta, Malta, the richly ornamented 1740s Baroque limestone building. Present-day clean restored stone appearance with all modern street and roof fittings excluded. This is exterior architectural sculpture, not a museum display or artwork reproduction.
Camera and framing: a plausible real camera at the foot of the entrance stairs, looking slightly upward toward the two-storey central facade, near axial with mild vertical perspective. The entire central DOOR PORTAL, the stone military trophy decoration surrounding and above that portal, the small bust directly ABOVE THE DOOR and BELOW the central upper-storey window, and the upper sculpted pediment/crest all fit INSIDE THE SAME landscape frame with margin. The building takes most of the frame; small blue sky area above. Show a short portion of the honey limestone entrance stair podium at the bottom. Do not cut off the portal, sculpture, crest or upper pediment.
Architecture: warm honey-colored Maltese limestone blockwork, restrained weathering and real grain, a slightly projecting central bay, freestanding carved columns flanking the doorway, layered Baroque moldings, pilasters, continuous cornice, recessed windows. A central upper-storey window aligns vertically over the doorway. Quiet dark green wooden shutters are visible on adjacent windows toward the lower edges.
Main details: a clearly STONE-CARVED, sculptural military TROPHY GROUP at the portal, made of inert swords, spear shafts, cannon forms, round drum forms, rolled and folded carved flags and pennants. All of these are limestone architectural carving attached to the facade, not actual usable weapons, fabric flags or flags on modern poles. The folded flags have no insignia. This original arrangement should evoke period architectural ornament without reproducing exact sculptural compositions. Stone carving has worn edges, deep recesses and believable shadows.
Bust location and material: immediately above the door on the central portal cornice, BELOW the upper central window, place ONE VERY SMALL dark patinated BRONZE sculptural bust with generic early-18th-century dress. The bust is clearly an architectural metal sculpture with a dull dark green-brown patina, hard sculpted forms, no skin tones and no living human. The face has only small distant weathered generic forms and must be impossible to identify as any actual person. Do not reproduce the face of any named historic or living person or any museum portrait/bust. Keep the bust at roughly 4 percent of image height, subordinate to the architectural carvings. There is NO bust on the rooftop, facade summit, upper pediment or above the upper window.
Upper ornaments: above the central window and in the crowning curved Baroque pediment, use original GENERIC carved heraldic-style stone cartouches with scrollwork and plain shield shapes. They are approximate decorative architecture, not exact coats of arms, branding or copied artwork. No letters, numerals, inscriptions, readable seals or monograms.
Style and light: photograph-like real camera material rendering, natural clear daylight, soft realistic shadows, restrained warm limestone and dark green colors against a normal blue sky. Real stone grain and bronze patina, calm believable exposure and natural optical detail. No HDR, no cinematic lighting or grading, no excessive saturation, no glossy CGI or illustrated/painted appearance.
Avoid: any people or human figures, recognizable person likeness, lifelike portrait faces, tourists, vehicles, actual modern flags or flagpoles, antennas, wires, cameras, modern fittings, signage, readable words, letters, numerals, plaques, logos, watermarks, captions, borders or frames.
